CROSS-SECTIONAL MOMENTUM — the factor that forced finance textbooks to re-examine "market efficiency."

Here's the complete logic. No black box:

🔹 Rank — every month, rank your universe by trailing 6-month return. Top decile (10%) are the winners. Bottom decile are the losers.

🔹 Skip — exclude the most recent month from the look-back. This avoids short-term reversal and bid-ask bounce — a step most retail strategies miss.

🔹 Long-short — go long the winners, short the losers, equal-weight, dollar-neutral. You're not predicting the market direction; you're trading relative strength.

🔹 Overlapping cohorts — instead of rebuilding the whole book every month, run 6 rolling baskets in parallel. Only 1/6 of the portfolio turns over each month. Lower costs, smoother returns.

🔹 Rebalance — monthly. Fully mechanical. Zero discretion, zero forecasting.

This is the original Jegadeesh-Titman relative-strength engine (Journal of Finance, 1993) — out-of-sample confirmed in 2001, codified into the Carhart UMD factor, and refined for crash management by Daniel & Moskowitz (JFE, 2016).
